task.description: Implement Letflow.Entities.Record.Projector (replay_record/3, rebuild_projection/2) exactly per the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved design doc, plus a full ExUnit test file covering REQ-229's 6 acceptance criteria.

result.note: New module lib/letflow/entities/record/projector.ex (Letflow.Entities.Record.Projector) implements replay_record/3 and rebuild_projection/2 exactly per design doc req229-entity-record-projection-replay.md, sharing one private fold_record_events/3 (@doc false) between both public functions, matching Letflow.Engine.Reconstruction's own fold-per-event-type precedent. The DELETE-case fold rule (the exact defect CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR caught in the design's earlier rework) is implemented correctly: field_values carried forward unchanged, entity_def_version re-decoded from the DELETE event's own payload via Base.decode16!/2, never carried forward from the pre-delete value. No migration, no schema change, no route/controller, no query DSL added -- confirmed via `git diff --stat 9613d348 -- .` showing only the new lib/letflow/entities/record/projector.ex, its test file, and this run's own handoff/design docs (zero lib/letflow_web/** paths touched, AC5). New test file test/letflow/entities/record/projector_test.exs, 10 tests, all passing, covering AC1 (create+2updates replay matches entity_record_latest), AC2 (DELETE-ending stream reflects deletion correctly, PLUS a dedicated test directly targeting the entity_def_version DELETE-case defect class by crafting a raw event stream via EventStore.append_multi/3 with a different entity_def_version hex on the DELETE event than the prior CREATE/UPDATE events, confirming the fold re-decodes from the DELETE event's own payload, not the pre-delete value), AC3 (rebuild_projection/2 restores exactly what replay_record/3 independently computes after artificially corrupting entity_record_latest rows for one entity type via Repo.update_all, plus an entity_type_not_found case and a corrupt-stream-aborts-only-that-type case), AC4 (tenant-scoped rebuild -- tenant A's rebuild does not touch tenant B's corrupted rows), AC5 (git diff --stat assertion, structural). Real command output: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> clean, no warnings, 'Generated letflow app'. `mix format --check-formatted` -> clean (both new files reformatted once via `mix format` before this check passed). `mix test test/letflow/entities/record/projector_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 12.8 seconds ... Result: 10 passed', 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/entities/` (regression) -> 'Result: 94 passed', 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/event_store/` (regression) -> 'Result: 150 passed', 0 failures. Full-repo `mix test` was not run to completion in this turn -- it exceeded the 120s foreground timeout on this large suite and was not required by this task's own instructions, which scoped regression to entities/ and event_store/ only; TEST-RUNNER should run the full suite before this requirement is marked done. DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (documented in Projector's own moduledoc and the test file's moduledoc, not silently worked around): Letflow.Entities.Definitions.get_definition_by_name/2 (already-shipped REQ-226 code, outside this module's scope) runs Repo.one/2 against `where: e.name == ^name` with no status/order/limit filter; entity_definitions' only uniqueness constraint is (tenant_id, name, logical_shape_version), so creating+activating a second definition version under the same name (the literal way to 'advance the entity definition to a new version') leaves two rows sharing that name, and every subsequent get_definition_by_name/2 call for that name -- including inside delete_record/2's own fetch_active_definition/2 -- raises Ecto.MultipleResultsError rather than a clean {:error, _} tuple. This blocked doing the AC2 defect test literally via Definitions.create_definition/2 + activate_definition/4 a second time; the test instead crafts the raw event stream directly via EventStore.append_multi/3 (bypassing the separately-broken code path) to produce the identical on-the-wire shape a real version advance would, exercising the exact same fold logic under test. Flagged for REVIEWER; not fixed here (out of ELIXIR-DEV's owned scope for this requirement). Also flagged in Projector's moduledoc: Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 never actually returns {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} (only {:error, :invalid_schema_name}), so that variant in replay_error()/rebuild_error() is currently dead code, kept only for design-doc parity.
